assessment_objectives.objective: cryptographic uses are identified / defined.
assessment_objectives.scf_defined_parameters: at a minimum, encryption and decryption of data, hashing, random number generation, key generation, generation of one-time passwords (OTPs) for multi-factor authentication and cryptographic protocols such as TLS, SSH and HTTPS

assessment_objectives.objective: cryptographic mechanisms intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of sensitive / regulated data are identified.
organization-defined types of cryptography are implemented to protect the confidentiality of sensitive / regulated data.
as necessary for compliance requirements, FIPS-validated cryptography is employed to protect the confidentiality of sensitive / regulated data.
security critical or essential software is defined.
root of trust mechanisms or cryptographic signatures are identified.
the integrity of security critical or essential software is verified using root of trust mechanisms or cryptographic signatures.
cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive / regulated data during transmission.
assessment_objectives.scf_defined_parameters: no lower than Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2, or a protocol of equivalent or greater cryptographic strength

assessment_objectives.objective: cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive / regulated data while in storage.
assessment_objectives.scf_defined_parameters: no weaker than Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) with a 128-bit key, or a cipher of equivalent or greater strength

assessment_objectives.objective: cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to detect unauthorized changes to software.
cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to detect unauthorized changes to firmware.
cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to detect unauthorized changes to information.
cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission.
cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of CUI while in storage.
the types of cryptography for protecting the confidentiality of CUI are defined.
the following types of cryptography are implemented to protect the confidentiality of CUI: <A.03.13.11.ODP[01]: types of cryptography>.
assessment_objectives.org_defined_parameters:
US DoD ODP Value: FIPS Validated Cryptography
(https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/Cryptographic-ModuleValidation-Program/Validated-Modules)

assessment_objectives.objective: cryptographic protections management operations are conducted according to documented policies, standards, procedures and/or other organizational directives.
resources are provided to support cryptographic protections management operations, including at a minimum: people, processes, technologies, data and facilities.
responsibility and authority for the performance of cryptographic protections management-related activities are assigned to designated personnel.
personnel performing cryptographic protections management-related activities have the skills and knowledge needed to perform their assigned duties.
